I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation, because I know it well, it fits the local climate and land, and it spreads my work across the year without taking too much risk. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage that carefully through spring with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations if water is available, and limited pesticide use only when pressure is obvious. After the wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away, using better seed so emergence is even and yield is more reliable. I will not make the plan too complicated with many crops, because I want something I can manage myself with stable returns, lower labor pressure, and familiar field practices.
